synth.notes:
Single horizontal mirror axis on a 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks; ACTION5 cycles the selection axis -> pieces (largest first) -> axis; A1/A2 move the selection up/down 3 cells, A3/A4 move a piece left/right 3 cells (no-op for the axis).
Each piece block not on axis row a reflects to row 2a-b in both directions, skipping off-board rows and blocks covered by a piece. The step-71 case is a piece on/below the axis reflecting upward. The axis is never blocked by pieces.
The global-counter hypothesis was refuted: the counter has no pixels and never changes in any transition.
Rendering: draw layers wall<target<reflection<piece; a hole shows the topmost solid pixel below it, else the topmost hole fill (selected = 0, reflection = 4). Then re-extract: walls and pieces are 4-connected components of their colour plus 0-dots, ranked by (x,y) counting dot-only components; reflections use colour 4 only; each target sprite is its own object.
